content.direction: A warm, lived-in kid's bedroom shared by two young brothers in a mid-2000s suburban Texas home on a sunny late afternoon. Chunky, softly rounded furniture and well-worn surfaces make the room feel loved and a little messy, with rumpled bedding, scuffed wood and sun-warmed air. A low wooden bunk bed with rumpled dusty-blue and mustard bedding stands along the rear wall beneath a ceiling dotted with small glow-in-the-dark stars. A chunky old tube television with a curved glass screen sits on a low wooden stand in the rear-right corner, glowing with soft colour only and no figures, with a generic dark game box and two tangled controllers spilling onto the rug in front of it. The centre of the floor is a faded patterned rug holding a half-played battle of chunky picture-only trading cards with sunny-yellow backs marked only with simple starburst shapes, plus open binders packed with sleeved cards and small rubber-banded stacks. A small wooden desk along the left wall holds a chunky toy microscope, a big magnifying glass, a kid chemistry set with chunky jars of coloured liquid, and a neat row of plain garden rocks, while the wall above is crowded with taped-up kid drawings of ringed planets and bubbling beakers made as pictures only. A wooden dresser on the right wall holds three spare pairs of chunky kid sunglasses, a school backpack slumps by the closet door, small sneakers lie kicked off beside the rug, and simple toys peek from under the beds. A folded geometric-patterned prayer rug and a string of smooth prayer beads rest on a low shelf by the closet, and worn spots and scuffs mark the floor and furniture edges. Slatted blinds over the left-wall window throw strong striped sunlight across the bedding and rug. Every card back, drawing, book cover, box, screen and fabric shape is blank of any words, letters, numbers, logos or familiar characters. Layout: the bunk bed runs along the rear wall, the desk and drawings line the left wall beneath the blind-covered window, the television stand anchors the rear-right, and the dresser and low shelf stand along the right wall. Open floor stays clear in the centre, with a standing spot screen-left and a simple wooden chair angled inward screen-right facing each other across the rug, each with a calm clear stretch of wall behind its future face. The camera sits at child eye level near the doorway, framing a medium-wide view with room for a slow straight push toward a medium two-shot. Light: warm late-afternoon Texas sun through slatted blinds, strong and readable with soft striped shadows. Bounce: warm bounce off sandy walls and honey wood. Practicals: one small shaded bedside lamp, off. Haze: no. Palette: muted warm honey wood, sandy cream and dusty blue at roughly five to one. Accent: saturated sunny yellow on generic trading-card backs and small toy science details. Film accent kept out: saturated violet-purple, not used anywhere in room.
